title: Armero tragedy
summary: On 13 November 1985, the Nevado del Ruiz volcano in Colombia erupted, melting its summit glaciers and generating lahars that raced down river valleys. The town of Armero, built on historic lahar deposits 45 km away, was engulfed around 11:30 p.m., killing approximately 23,000 people. It was the second-deadliest volcanic disaster of the 20th century and Colombia's worst natural disaster.

uncertainty.note: Eruption began 9:09 p.m. local time 13 Nov 1985; lahars hit Armero ~11:30 p.m. same night.

where.historical_name: Armero, Tolima Department, Republic of Colombia

importance.justification: Second-deadliest volcanic disaster of the 20th century; prompted creation of volcano monitoring programs worldwide.

audience_note: Record describes a mass-casualty disaster with graphic details of victims trapped in lahars.

reviewer_note: Death toll varies across sources (20,000–25,000); outline uses ~23,000 from USGS and Wikipedia FA. Coordinates are for modern Armero-Guyabal; the original town site was buried. No animation included as the event is a single-night disaster at one location.
